title: 'No One But God and My Fans': Dhanush Sidesteps BJP-Backing Talk Amid Political Debut Buzz
excerpt: The Tamil star's one-line response, reported by News18, lands after a lotus motif on fan-gathering gifts, an RSS-meeting report and a Congress allegation of an 'Operation D' — while his five-film slate points away from politics.
body:
• Actor Dhanush has pushed back on speculation about a BJP-backed political debut, saying he answers to "no one but God and my fans," News18 reported.
  • The buzz grew after a lotus motif was spotted on silver lamps gifted at his fan association's Diwali gathering; the association said the mark was the silversmith's trademark, not a party symbol.
  • Congress leader Manickam Tagore has alleged a BJP-RSS plan — dubbed "Operation D" — behind the speculation; TVK's Aadhav Arjuna has also criticised scripted celebrity entries, while DMK and AIADMK figures say Dhanush is free to enter politics if he wishes.
  • Dhanush has announced no political plans, and his film slate — five films lined up, per director Rajkumar Periyasamy — points the other way for now.

Tamil star Dhanush has responded to a fortnight of speculation about a possible political debut and alleged BJP backing with a short, pointed answer: he is accountable to "no one but God and my fans," News18 reported. The actor has made no political announcement, launched no party, and — on the evidence of his own schedule — has five films to finish first.

How the speculation started

The latest round of buzz traces to the reorganisation of Dhanush's fan association, renamed Dhanush Narpani Iyakkam (Dhanush Welfare Movement), and to a Diwali-season gathering of its women's wing on Chennai's outskirts, where more than 2,500 supporters met the actor. Silver Kamakshi lamps gifted to attendees carried a lotus motif at the base — and because the lotus is the BJP's election symbol, the gift set off a fresh wave of talk about a Delhi-backed entry, along with reports of an unannounced party name, "Tamilaga Ezhuchi Kazhagam," doing the rounds. The fan association clarified that the lotus was the trademark of the silver merchants who made the lamps and carried no political meaning.

The restructured fan network itself invites the comparison everyone in Tamil Nadu is making: actor Vijay's fan organisation evolved into the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and carried him to the chief ministership. Reports of Dhanush meeting a senior RSS functionary in August and September added fuel.

The political crossfire

Reactions split along predictable lines. Tamil Nadu Congress leader Manickam Tagore alleged a BJP-RSS effort to float a new celebrity face in the state, calling it "Operation D." TVK leader Aadhav Arjuna criticised actors entering politics on a script written by "Delhi bigwigs," and figures in Vijay's camp have dismissed the idea that another star can shortcut the years of grassroots work behind TVK's rise. Senior DMK and AIADMK voices, by contrast, have said Dhanush — like Vijay before him — is entitled to enter politics if he chooses.

"No one but God and my fans."

— Dhanush, on speculation about his political plans, as reported by News18

Why the film slate matters

The strongest counter-evidence to an imminent debut is Dhanush's diary. Rajkumar Periyasamy, who is directing the actor's next film, Om, has noted that Dhanush had already begun shooting another film before Om's release and has five films lined up — a slate that would occupy three to four years. Tamil Nadu's cinema-to-politics pipeline is real, and Dhanush's family history keeps the talk alive: he was previously married to Aishwaryaa Rajinikanth, daughter of Rajinikanth, whose own political flirtations ran for decades. But as of this week, the only confirmed fact is the speculation itself — and the actor's one-line answer to it.
nri_angle: Tamil cinema's politics pipeline is followed closely by the Tamil diaspora; Dhanush is its biggest current question mark.
author: Diaspora Desk
